transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Um… I guess what finally pushed me to come in is work stuff. I’m an accountant, and after audits or even mentorship events, I’ll start these follow-up items with every intention of finishing them—like the final email, a review note, or a form—and then somehow days later I find out it never actually got done.

It’s embarrassing because in my head I did it, or I was right there about to do it, and then it’s just… not finished. And then I’m scrambling, or someone’s waiting on me. It’s been happening enough that I thought, okay, I probably need to talk to someone instead of just buying another planner or making another color-coded list.
Does this kind of difficulty with follow-through happen only at work, or do you notice similar patterns in other areas of your life, like personal projects, household tasks, or social commitments?

Yeah, I mean… the clearest place I see it is work. That’s really what pushed me to make the appointment. Like after an audit or a mentorship event, I’ll start the follow-up stuff thinking, okay, I just need to send the final email or write the review note or finish the form, and then somehow a few days go by and I realize it never actually got done.

It’s not usually that I don’t care about it—I really do mean to finish it. I’ll even sort of remember being right on the edge of doing it, if that makes sense. But then it’s just… still sitting there unfinished, and someone is waiting on me. That’s the part that’s been getting harder to brush off.
When you're trying to finish these tasks, do you find yourself easily distracted by other things, or does it feel more like you just lose track of the steps needed to finish them?

Yeah, it’s more the distracted thing, I think. Like if I’m reviewing an audit file and a Slack message pops up, or someone is talking outside my office, I can get pulled completely away from what I was doing.

And it’s not always even external—sometimes I’ll have a random thought, like something about marathon training or whether I need new shoes, and then suddenly I’m looking that up or thinking through my running schedule, and the audit file is just… still there. Then later I’m like, wait, I never finished that section.
Do you often feel restless, as if you need to be moving or doing something, even in situations where others might feel comfortable just sitting still?

Yes, definitely. Sitting still through a long review can feel… weirdly physical, like there’s pressure building up inside me. I’ll be trying to focus, and then I just feel like I need to get up.

Sometimes I’ll stand up to walk to the printer, even if I don’t really need to, or I’ll invent some reason to move around for a minute. It’s funny, because as an accountant you’d think I’d be good at just sitting with documents, and I can do it, but it feels uncomfortable after a while—like my body is saying, “Okay, enough, move.”
Looking back, did you have similar difficulties with staying focused or finishing tasks when you were younger, like in school or with chores at home?

Yeah… looking back, I think it was there pretty early. Even in elementary school, my report cards would say things like I was bright, but I lost assignments or rushed through and missed little details. Or I’d talk out of turn and need reminders to actually finish the work.

My mom still brings it up sometimes—she jokes that I could get an A on the test but forget the whole project sitting in my backpack. Which is funny now, kind of, but also… yeah, that pattern sounds pretty familiar.
Do you find yourself struggling to finish tasks or losing focus even in everyday routines, like chores at home, running errands, or even while watching a show or reading something?

Yeah, I think so. It’s maybe most obvious with longer things. Like I can start a long client meeting totally engaged, taking notes, following along, and then at some point I realize I’ve been staring at the screen but I didn’t actually hear the last few minutes.

That happened in one of those AI-tool trainings too—everyone’s talking about how it’s going to change audit workflows, and I was interested, honestly, because I do think some of that stuff is useful, though also a little overhyped maybe… but anyway, I suddenly realized I’d missed a whole chunk of what the trainer was saying. I was still sitting there looking attentive, but my mind had just slipped off somewhere else.
Do you often feel frustrated or upset with yourself when you realize you’ve missed something or didn’t finish a task, even if you meant to?

Yes. I get really frustrated with myself, honestly. That’s kind of what pushed me to make this appointment.

It’s not that I don’t care—I’ll leave an audit or a mentorship event with every intention of doing the follow-up items. I’ll even start them. And then days later I’ll realize the final email never got sent, or a review note is still sitting unfinished, or some form I meant to submit just… didn’t actually get done.

And then I’m mad at myself because it feels so avoidable. Like, I meant to do it. I can picture myself thinking, “I’ll finish that in a minute,” and then somehow it just disappears until it’s a problem.
Do you often struggle to start tasks, even when you know they’re important or when you have a clear plan for how to do them?

I’m not totally sure how to separate “can’t start” from “I get pulled into something else,” if that makes sense.

Like, if I have a plan, sometimes I’ll sit down with all the right stuff open and then somehow I’m checking one related email, and then that leads to another thing, and—sorry, I know that’s not exactly what you asked. I guess I do notice there are times where I know something matters, but getting myself to actually begin feels weirdly harder than it should.

But I don’t know if I’d say it’s every task. Sometimes if there’s pressure or it’s urgent, I can start. It’s more like… the starting line is sticky, maybe. Does that make sense?
Do you often feel irritable or have trouble managing frustration, especially when things don’t go as planned or when you’re trying to focus on something important?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I get annoyed like anyone does, especially if something gets derailed, but I don’t know that I’d say it’s a major thing I’ve noticed.

Sometimes I’m more frustrated with the situation than angry, if that makes sense. Like if I’m trying to get something done and there are interruptions, I can feel myself getting tense—but then again, in accounting there are always interruptions, especially around deadlines, and everyone’s tense then. Sorry, that’s probably not a very clear answer.

I guess I haven’t really thought of irritability as the main problem. It’s more that I notice I’m struggling and then I get frustrated after the fact.

Outside of work and structured tasks, do you find yourself losing track of things or getting distracted in more casual situations—like while having a conversation, watching a movie, or even just trying to relax?

Yeah, I think so. I notice it most at work, but it’s not only work.

Like if I’m trying to review an audit file, even a Slack ping or someone talking outside my office can completely pull me off track. Or I’ll be reading something and then suddenly I’m thinking about marathon training—like what pace I’m supposed to run this weekend—and then I realize I have no idea what I just read.

In conversations it can happen too, though I try to hide it. I’ll be listening and then some random thought catches, and I have to kind of mentally rewind. It’s embarrassing, honestly.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking through the consequences, like interrupting others, making sudden decisions, or saying things you later regret?

Yeah… I think that happens, mostly with interrupting. I don’t usually think of myself as making big sudden decisions or anything, but in conversations—especially with junior auditors—I’ll jump in before they’ve finished.

It’s like I can see where they’re going, or the answer pops into my head, and it feels urgent in that moment, so I blurt it out. Then afterward I realize I kind of cut them off. I don’t mean to be rude, but I can hear myself doing it sometimes and still don’t stop fast enough.
Do you notice these same issues with distraction or losing focus in social settings, such as when you're at dinner with friends or attending a gathering?

Yes, it can happen there too, though I guess I notice it more clearly at work because there’s something I’m supposed to be doing.

Like, the same kind of thing happens if I’m trying to follow a conversation and there’s noise nearby, or even just some random thought pops in. At work it’s really obvious—if I’m reviewing an audit file, a Slack ping or someone talking outside my office can completely derail me. Or I’ll suddenly be thinking about marathon training, like what pace I’m supposed to run, and then I’ve lost the thread of what I was doing.

In social situations it’s a little harder to describe because everyone’s talking and there’s food and side conversations, so I sort of tell myself that’s normal. But yes, I can lose focus the same way.
Do you find it hard to stay focused or complete tasks even during leisure activities, like cooking a meal, organizing your space, or doing something you enjoy?

Yeah, I mean… yes, it can happen even when it’s something I’m interested in. Not always in the same way as chores, but I’ll start off totally engaged.

Like in a long client meeting, or even one of those AI-tool trainings we’ve been doing lately—I’m interested, I’m looking at the screen, I’m nodding along—and then after a while my mind just sort of… slips somewhere else. And then I realize I missed the last few minutes even though I was sitting there the whole time.

It’s frustrating because from the outside I probably look like I’m paying attention. And sometimes I am at first. It just doesn’t always hold.
Do you often feel emotionally overwhelmed or have strong mood shifts, even over small things, that make it harder to focus or get things done?

I’m not sure I’d describe it as strong mood shifts, no. I mean, I can get stressed like anyone, especially when there’s a lot going on, but I don’t know that it’s sudden emotional swings over small things.

Sometimes I have trouble telling what’s “overwhelmed” versus just… a normal busy day, you know? Like if I’ve got work stuff and then I’m thinking about errands or dinner or whatever, it can all feel like a lot, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean. So I guess I haven’t really noticed mood shifts as the main thing.

I’m not sure I’d describe it as strong mood shifts, no. I mean, I can get stressed like anyone, especially when there’s a lot going on, but I don’t know that it’s sudden emotional swings over small things.

Sometimes I have trouble telling what’s “overwhelmed” versus just… a normal busy day, you know? Like if I’ve got work stuff and then I’m thinking about errands or dinner or whatever, it can all feel like a lot, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean. So I guess I haven’t really noticed mood shifts as the main thing.

inference.note: The patient's symptoms of distraction, difficulty completing tasks, restlessness, and impulsivity have been consistently present since childhood and are not limited to specific contexts, which aligns with ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation. There is insufficient evidence for significant mood shifts, anxiety, or other primary mood or anxiety disorders as the core issue.
